correctness.rationale: Reconstructed sharp upper bound: the undeleted power P^k is not Lyndon because suffix P^(k-1) is also a prefix, so any optimal length is at most kp-1. For a single deletion, the first or final cycle lexicographically dominates comparisons at its altered run; all interior-copy deletions retain a suffix equal to the initial P and fail. Minimum-letter internal suffixes and terminal-run shortening are treated. At every nonterminal run, exactly one of ascent/descending cases qualifies, giving p positions and q distinct Parikh vectors. Independent literal suffix-checking verified all predicted winning positions on 232 exhaustive small parameter profiles (q=2..4, run lengths=1..2, k=2,3), including nonmonotone letter permutations.

evidence: Bannai et al provide a general optimization procedure, with a distinct-letter special case, not an all-optimizer repeated-run theorem.
